notes:
The owner's catalog of every item: its category and subcategory, whether it is in the game, planned or cut, and the design intent the code does not carry — the 1–5 ratings, what recycling would give back, and the bench it is planned for. Imported from Notion's Items and Workbenches tables on 2026-09-10. The game never reads this file.

For an item in the game, the numbers that matter live in its own table (WEAPONS, RES, …) and this row is the plan around them. For a planned item this row is all there is, so its proposed recipe and stats live here until it is built; building it means giving it a row in its real table under the same id.

bench_plan is the planned bench split (Player Menu, Basic, Advanced, Tech, and a Recycler that crafts nothing). None of those benches exists yet: today the game has by hand, the Workbench, Workbench II and the Chemistry Station.

Player Menu (bench 0): The default. No bench needed, and only a limited set: stone tools, cordage, a torch, a bow and arrows, bandages, the first clothes. Carrying a Stone Hammer lifts any recipe flagged hammer up to bench-1 work by hand (the work you could do on a flat rock). It never lifts further, so a hammer can never make a gun.

rows.name: Tire Iron
rows.notes: Car trunks.

rows.notes: Toolboxes, garages.

rows.name: Baseball Bat

rows.name: Police Baton
rows.notes: Police lockers.

rows.name: Reinforced Bat

rows.name: Stone Hammer

rows.name: Cleaver
rows.notes: Kitchens, stores.

rows.name: Hunting Knife
rows.notes: Cabins, gun shops, footlockers.

rows.name: Katana
rows.notes: Display cases, pawn shops. Rare. The top of the bladed line: fast, high damage, no crowd control.

rows.name: Kitchen Knife
rows.notes: Kitchens. Fast, low damage. Cuts cordage like the Stone Knife.

rows.name: Kukri
rows.notes: Military, footlockers.

rows.name: Stone Knife
rows.notes: Cuts cordage: fiber becomes cloth.

rows.name: Camping Axe
rows.notes: Cabins, farm stores. Between the Hatchet and the Fire Axe.

rows.name: Fire Axe
rows.notes: The metal tool tier: nearly twice the hatchet at trees.

rows.name: Hatchet
rows.notes: The first gate: no hatchet, no wood, no workbench.

rows.name: Splitting Axe
rows.notes: Lumber yards, log piles. The best wood-chopper; slow to swing.

rows.name: Garden Spear
rows.notes: Garden sheds, hardware stores.

rows.name: Makeshift Knife Spear
rows.notes: A knife lashed to a pole.
rows.recipe: 6 Sticks, 4 Fiber, 1 Kitchen Knife or Stone Knife (proposal)

rows.name: Metal Spear
rows.notes: The top of the polearm line. Craft only.

rows.name: Pitchfork
rows.notes: Barns.

rows.name: Scythe
rows.notes: Opens thickets. The widest swing in the game.

rows.name: Wooden Spear
rows.notes: Reach. The first polearm, made from nothing.

rows.name: Large Wrench
rows.notes: Industrial, junkyards. A pipe wrench the length of your arm.

rows.name: Makeshift Concrete Club
rows.notes: A lump of concrete on a rebar handle. Heavy, cheap, ugly.

rows.name: Maul
rows.notes: Lumber yards. Splitting maul: slower than the sledge, hits harder.

rows.name: Sledgehammer
rows.notes: Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Stone Pickaxe
rows.notes: Opens boulders.

rows.name: Revolver
rows.notes: Always have one. Slower and louder than the M9, hits harder, no magazine to find.

rows.name: Double-Barrel Shotgun
rows.notes: Get off me. Two shots then a long reload. Rural houses and cabins.

rows.name: Pump Shotgun
rows.notes: Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Semi-Auto Shotgun
rows.notes: The crowd answer, and the loudest thing short of an LMG. Police and gun shops.

rows.name: Bolt-Action Rifle
rows.notes: One shot, one walker, then a whole second to work the bolt.

rows.name: Hunting Rifle
rows.notes: Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Lever-Action Rifle
rows.notes: Make the shot count. Cabins, barns, farmhouses.

rows.name: Compact SMG
rows.notes: Oh crap. Fits in a bag, empties a magazine in two seconds.

rows.name: Scrap SMG
rows.notes: Craft only. Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: AK-Style Rifle
rows.notes: The AR's rougher twin: louder and less accurate, but it never jams.

rows.name: AR-Style Rifle
rows.notes: Workhorse. Good at everything, rare, and hungry for rifle rounds.

rows.name: Military Carbine
rows.notes: The endgame gun. Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Marksman Rifle
rows.notes: Base defence from the Watchtower. Terrible when something is already on top of you.

rows.name: Scoped Hunting Rifle
rows.notes: Reach out and touch something. A Hunting Rifle plus optics; a modification rather than a new gun.

rows.name: Compound Bow
rows.notes: Stay quiet. Harder-hitting than the Hunting Bow, and arrows are recoverable.

rows.name: Crossbow
rows.notes: Near-silent and it hits like a rifle. The reload is the cost.

rows.name: Hunting Bow
rows.notes: The quiet answer to a gun, reachable in the first ten minutes.

rows.name: Flamethrower
rows.notes: Burns Fuel and sets the world alight. Fire already spreads in game, so watch your own treeline.

rows.name: Grenade Launcher
rows.notes: End game, military only. Needs its own ammunition, which should stay very rare.

rows.name: LMG
rows.notes: End game, military only. Sustained fire builds your own horde while you use it.

rows.name: Flashlight
rows.notes: Eats Batteries. You find those before you can make them.

rows.name: Torch
rows.notes: The first night's answer. Burns itself up, so you keep remaking it.

rows.name: Combat Helmet
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: Riot Helmet
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: Plate Carrier
rows.notes: The biggest single piece of armour. Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Riot Armor
rows.notes: Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Arm Guards
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: Tactical Gloves
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: Combat Trousers
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: Assault Boots
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: Combat Boots
rows.notes: Find only.

rows.name: 9mm Rounds
rows.notes: Pistol, SMG, and the Auto Turret eats it from the stash.

rows.name: Rifle Rounds
rows.notes: Rifle, carbine, and the tower Sniper Rifle. Currently needs the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Arrows
rows.notes: For the Hunting Bow and the tower Arrows armament.

rows.name: Bandage
rows.notes: You start with two.

rows.name: Corn
rows.notes: 4 Corn + 2 Cloth make 8 Rations at a Basic bench. That is the reason farming exists: the crew eats Rations out of the Supply Stash, so a corn patch is what stops a base needing a supply run to stay fed. Ranked above potatoes for the quick-eat key, so a tap of F never eats the corn you were going to turn into rations.

rows.name: Herbs
rows.notes: 4 Herbs + 1 Cloth make 2 Medical at a Basic bench — two an in-game day against a pharmacy's eight to sixteen in one search, so a long siege stops running you out of bandages and serum without pharmacies losing their reason to exist. This is the balance number most likely to want moving. Also the seasoning in the garden Hot Meal.

rows.name: Potatoes
rows.notes: Grown in a Raised Bed from Potato Eyes. The bulk crop and the cooking staple: 3 Potatoes + 1 Herbs + 1 Clean Water + 2 Wood make TWO Hot Meals at a Basic bench, against one from three Rations — cooking what you grew beats cooking what you found, which is the payoff for the days it took.

rows.name: Rations
rows.notes:
Survivor upkeep: one per survivor per minute, eaten from the Supply Stash. The player never eats.

SECOND RECIPE, 2026-09-10: 4 Corn and 2 Cloth also make 8 at a Basic bench, and that is the whole reason farming exists — a corn patch is what stops a base needing a supply run to stay fed. The Recipe column holds one recipe, so it still shows the Ration Pack; how the table should carry an item with two ways to make it is a question for you, not something a sync should decide.

rows.name: Lockpick
rows.notes: Opens locked cars. May snap, and snapping is heard.

rows.name: Compost
rows.notes: The everyday feed. One dose per bed, and it can go in after planting — feeding yesterday's crop still counts. Fertilizer is yield and not speed, because the grow clock is what a player plans the day around. Subcategory is Raw as the nearer of the two Materials options; it is crafted, not scavenged.

rows.name: Fiber
rows.notes: Binding for tools, and cordage: 10 Fiber becomes 4 Cloth with a knife.

rows.name: Mutagen Sludge
rows.notes: Made at the CHEMISTRY STATION. Two things this row cannot say properly yet: the Chemistry Station has no row in the Workbenches table (it is a separate gate from the bench ladder on purpose — no amount of upgrading a workbench ever produces this), and Raw Brain Matter has no Items row, so the Ingredients link is short one. Spends the brain matter that holds the Mutation meter down: more food for less of what keeps you human, which is the game's own bargain in a vegetable patch.

rows.name: Sticks
rows.notes: Every stone tool starts with these. Bonus drop from trees, bushes and thickets.

rows.name: Stone
rows.notes: Stone tools and the Stone Wall. Boulders need a pickaxe, loose rocks do not.

rows.name: Wood
rows.notes: The base building material. Trees need a hatchet, so a fresh game finds it in cabinets and log piles first.

rows.name: Batteries
rows.notes: What the Flashlight eats. Findable long before it is craftable, on purpose.

rows.name: Cloth
rows.notes: Bandages, clothes, armour padding, beds. Found everywhere soft, or cut from fiber with a knife.

rows.name: Corn Seed
rows.notes: The long crop and the one that pays: corn becomes Rations, and Rations are what the crew eats out of the Supply Stash. Twice a potato's time for roughly twice the reason.

rows.name: Electronics
rows.notes: Powers the tier-2 base: generator, turret, floodlight, and the bench upgrade.

rows.name: Fuel
rows.notes: Burned by the Generator and by cars. Also the Fire Arrows armament.

rows.name: Herb Seed
rows.notes: The medicine crop. Herbs become Medical at a Basic bench, slowly.

rows.name: Medical
rows.notes: Medical supplies. Medkits and ration packs. As of 2026-09-10 it is also farmable: 4 Herbs and 1 Cloth make 2 at a Basic bench. Deliberately a trickle — two an in-game day against a pharmacy's eight to sixteen in one search — so a long siege stops running you out of bandages and serum without pharmacies losing their reason to exist.

rows.name: Military
rows.notes: Military-grade components. Only from the checkpoint, footlockers and hospital cabinets. Gates the rifle, carbine and plate armour.

rows.name: Potato Eyes
rows.notes: Plant in a Raised Bed. Every harvest returns one seed of its own kind and sometimes a second, so a patch feeds itself once it is started — without that a farm dead-ends the first time the loot tables stop offering seed.

rows.name: Scrap
rows.notes: Sheet metal, the second base material. Everything metal costs it. Also what the Scrap Cannon fires.

rows.name: Weapon Parts
rows.notes: Springs, pins, barrels. The gate on every gun and every box of ammunition.

rows.name: Barricade
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. Cheap, fast, flimsy.

rows.name: Gate
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1.

rows.name: Reinforced Wall
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1.

rows.name: Steel Wall
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 2: needs the upgraded Workbench.

rows.name: Stone Wall
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. The wall you can raise before you own any metal tool.

rows.name: Wood Wall
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1.

rows.name: Steel Locker
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. Survives a raid that flattens a chest.

rows.name: Supply Stash
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. The base pantry: survivors and towers feed from it.

rows.name: Wooden Chest
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1.

rows.breaks_down_into: 25 Scrap, 14 Electronics, 3 Weapon Parts (salvage, in game)
rows.name: Auto Turret
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 2. Needs a powered Generator within 260px; eats 9mm from the stash.

rows.name: Spike Trap
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. Wears out.

rows.name: Watchtower
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. Post a survivor on it as a Sniper.

rows.name: Floodlight
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 2. Needs a powered Generator within 260px.

rows.name: Generator
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 2. Loud: raises Threat while running.

rows.name: Bedroll
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. Sets your respawn point; only the newest one is active.

rows.name: Bunk
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. No bunk, no recruit.

rows.name: Raised Bed
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. A seed slot, an optional feed slot and a water meter. Watered with Clean Water — the same bottle that buys the Hydrated buff, so drink it or grow with it is the decision. A dry bed stops growing and NEVER dies: forgetting it costs time, never the crop. Deliberately not a protect piece — a garden is not a fortification and must not widen the base radius or pull a raid at it. Salvaging one returns the seed and the feed; a brute through it does not.

rows.name: Advanced Bench
rows.notes:
Built from the Building menu. Metalwork: pipes, blades, firearms, ammunition, armour plates.

What it is for: Metalwork. Pipes, blades, firearms, ammunition, armour plates, lockpicks.

Takes over the metal half of the current Workbench (bench 1) and the guns and armour from the upgraded Workbench (bench 2; the upgrade costs 55 Scrap, 20 Electronics, 5 Weapon Parts). In-game items linked here currently live on one of those two.

rows.name: Basic Bench
rows.notes:
Built from the Building menu, which needs no bench. Unlocks the Basic crafting tab.

What it is for: The first bench. Wood, stone and cloth work: hafts and handles, bats, spears, the metal tools that need a wooden haft, medkits, ration packs.

Takes over the non-metal half of the single Workbench in the game today (bench 1 in config.gd). In-game items linked here currently live on that Workbench.

Build cost (proposal): 30 Wood, 18 Scrap (the cost of the current Workbench, as a starting point)
rows.recipe: 30 Wood, 18 Scrap (today's Workbench cost, as a starting point)

rows.name: Recycler
rows.notes:
Built from the Building menu. Breaks items down into base materials. Nothing is crafted at it.

What it is for: Breaks bigger things down into base materials. Nothing is crafted here. What each item gives back is on the item, under Breaks down into.

Not in the game yet. When it lands, every Breaks down into entry on the Items table becomes a recycling recipe.

rows.name: Tech Bench
rows.notes:
Built from the Building menu. Electronics and military-grade kit.

What it is for: Electronics and military-grade kit. Batteries, fuel, flashlights, SMGs and assault rifles: anything that eats Electronics or Military.

Takes over the electronics recipes from the current Workbench and upgraded Workbench. In-game items linked here currently need the upgraded Workbench (bench 2).

rows.name: Workbench
rows.notes: Build menu, tier 1. The single bench in the game today; the Benches table is the plan to split it up.

rows.name: Precision Parts
rows.notes: Levels 4 to 6 of a weapon. Only out of an instance, past its boss.

rows.name: Varsity Bat
rows.notes: The Coach's, 25% of the time. Cannot be mended or upgraded; lasts. A placeholder.

rows.name: Six-Shooter
rows.notes: The Coach's, 15% of the time. Cannot be mended or upgraded; lasts. A placeholder.
